risk_description: Forecast under-predicts a surge. Site team relies on it, does not open escalation beds or arrange extra discharge support in time. Patients wait longer in the Emergency Department.
who_could_be_affected: Patients waiting for a bed (mostly older and frailer); ED staff
evidence_so_far: 07_prototype_v0_3/backtest_site_level.csv (not yet analysed by pressure level); trial notes TN-01 and TN-04

risk_description: Forecast over-predicts. Planned operations are cancelled or staff are booked unnecessarily.
who_could_be_affected: Patients on waiting lists; hospital budget
evidence_so_far: None measured. 02_hospital_uk_kingsmere/elective_tci_list.csv shows who is cancelled today

risk_description: Forecast becomes a discharge target. Pressure to 'hit the number' leads to patients leaving before they are ready, late-evening discharges and readmissions.
who_could_be_affected: Older patients; people needing care packages; carers
evidence_so_far: Patient panel comments; flow_incident_log.csv has late-night discharge incidents. Link between pressure and readmission not analysed

risk_description: Forecast is used to reduce, cancel or redeploy nursing shifts ('the screen is green, send a nurse to Ward 20').
who_could_be_affected: Ward nurses and healthcare assistants; patients on the donor ward
evidence_so_far: Staff survey Q10; ward manager and staff-side interviews; trial note TN-02

risk_description: Automation bias: users act on the colour or the single number and stop applying local knowledge (infection closures, care-home embargoes, strikes).
evidence_so_far: Usability test task T3; no evidence yet from real use

risk_description: Model silently degrades after a local change: EPR migration, ward reconfiguration, change in how activity is recorded.
evidence_so_far: Three such changes at Kingsmere in three years (see data_notes_from_information_team.md)
current_controls: Monthly manual review of error (not yet scheduled)

risk_description: The thing we forecast may not be the thing users think it is: 'beds occupied' versus 'beds needed'.
Accuracy is worse for small units (children's ward, critical care, maternity, neonatal). Those services get a poorer tool or are left out.
who_could_be_affected: Children, pregnant women, critically ill patients; staff on those units

risk_description: Unequal impact: the consequences of pressure (cancellations, long waits, delayed discharge) may fall more heavily on some groups. A tool that optimises the average could entrench this.
who_could_be_affected: People in deprived areas; older people; minority ethnic groups; people without family support
evidence_so_far: Not analysed. Ethnicity is missing for a material share of records and recording changed with the EPR

risk_description: Re-identification: the extract has patient-level rows with exact age, postcode district, exact timestamps and a persistent pseudo-identifier.
evidence_so_far: Our DPIA draft calls the data 'anonymous'; the trust's IG lead disagrees (see data_sharing_correspondence.md)
current_controls: Access limited to 6 named staff; encrypted storage

risk_description: National data opt-out may not have been applied to the discovery extract.
who_could_be_affected: Patients who have opted out; the trust; the company

risk_description: Sensitive detail sits in free text and in linkable incident narratives (abbreviations in the Kenya register sample; incident summaries with spell IDs).
current_controls: Names and phone numbers removed before loading

risk_description: Use beyond the agreed purpose: the Kingsmere data-sharing agreement covers discovery and product research, not live operational use or training a commercial product for other customers.
Insecure transfer: hospital data sent outside the agreed channel (photographed registers via personal messaging app; spreadsheet by ordinary email).
Public trust: 'private company profits from NHS patient data'. A news story or freedom-of-information request during the pilot.
who_could_be_affected: The trust; the company; future public acceptance

risk_description: Marketing claims run ahead of evidence ('95% accurate', savings per hospital).
Regulatory status unclear (medical device? high-risk AI system?). A late finding would add cost and delay.
Clinical safety work depends on one part-time contractor; Horizon has no hazard log or safety case yet.
Transfer failure: a model shaped by UK data and UK ways of working gives confident, wrong output in Kenya or Indonesia (different diseases, seasons, data, strikes, room classes).
who_could_be_affected: Patients and staff at partner hospitals

risk_description: The tool adds reporting work for already stretched staff; data collection displaces care.
who_could_be_affected: Nurses and records officers, especially in Kenya

risk_description: Partner terms weaken control over data and model: donor wants hospital data for its own research (Kenya); vendor wants to host and brand the model (Indonesia).
Environmental footprint of training, hosting and devices.
The service is withdrawn after a pilot because the company cannot fund it, leaving a hospital that has changed how it works.
evidence_so_far: 01_company_wardline/financials_monthly.csv; history of ended pilots in Kisima County

risk_description: People who were not consulted (night staff, healthcare assistants, agency staff, patients in Indonesia) are affected by a tool designed around managers.
A user changes the manual 'beds open' field by mistake or on purpose; forecast shifts with no audit trail.
Wards learn to game the inputs (for example, delay recording discharges) so they are not asked to take outliers.
People believe 'AI is deciding who gets a bed'.
Bad input produces an absurd forecast that is displayed without a sanity check (duplicate day, missing feed, mis-keyed daily return).
evidence_so_far: Duplicate records after the EPR migration; typing errors in the manual daily return
